touches.text: Outline check: when a ticket is cast, the cheapest model reads it beside the outline sections it touches. A conflict, or an open question in those sections, becomes a [Q#n] at the outline line it bears on (0.6.2), and that open [Q#n] holds the ticket's build until it is answered. It reads the outline as it stands each time, so editing the outline costs nothing. WHY: a ticket that contradicts the outline builds something Akien did not intend, and the cheapest time to catch that is before the build. - CC

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead.

A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, because even the Laws rest finally on the core principles. Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).

outline_check: the outline check of 9.3.5.1. It reads one ticket beside the outline as it stands, and each conflict, or open question in a section the ticket touches, holds the ticket's build until answered. WHY: a ticket filed without anyone reading the outline should not reach a build unnoticed. - CC

The inspectors are not assumed correct; they are examined when they refuse. After a gate refuses, an LLM sets the refusing sieve's intention and why beside the ticket's intention and why and asks: is this sieve the best we can do right now? If yes, the ticket changes. If no, the sieve is fixed through its own ticket and proof. Either way the system improves. WHY: a disagreement becomes an update to an intention or its implementation, never a conversation about procedure. The sieves stay deterministic and never weigh a why; the LLM check comes only after a failure, and it is never a lock pick because it has no third outcome. Nothing passes a ticket over a red.

Fixit (bug): at BUILDME the ticket names the red it fixes (the proof), and that proof really is red on disk now. The fix may change the test case itself without a ruling: the proof's why names the ticket and says what it tests and why it changed, and names any tooth it removed. At PROVED it is sealed green and hollow-measured.
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Owns the inspectors and gates (9.4): everything in the code pipeline that checks. The exception is diagnostic_inspector, which is base's (17.1).

A ticket's plan is a plan, not a list of decisions: constraints, outcomes and resources. - Outcomes, not tasks: each is a claim a proof can check. An outcome hides the how. - Constraints: the bounds, and every how Akien is attached to (encapsulation, the bus as the only channel). - Order comes only from real dependencies (you can't test the bus envelope shape until the bus works), and those also set ticket order. - Resources: existing machines, tools and design patterns, named when they need stating. - A plan too big splits into tickets. Early steps can reshape later ones, so the whole is checked for coherence at the end. -amm
Test tiers: commit, hourly, daily and weekly. Each tier runs only what it must, so a commit needs only its own proofs and the long runs wait for the long tiers; nothing runs just in case.
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).
A proof that cannot go red without its build (its hollow is empty) stands only on Akien's answered approval, recorded as the hollow reading and re-read at clearance; any other empty hollow is red.
TOOLS: base, validation_store, proof_coverage, scratch, question, proof_discovery, chain, bus_client, artifact, system_word; machine build_inspector; db client.

How the TESTING database works. (1) The db proxy is the seam (4.3.1.5.1.4.1.1, 11.3.7): proofs, devices and tools never choose a database; the proxy chooses by session context. (2) The test runner sets the context, never the proof: bin/cairn test and the hollow run open every db session with context=testing, so a proof can neither forget it nor pick live (Law 4). (3) In testing context, writes go only to the TESTING database: same schema, rows from a reserved address range, so a testing address never collides with a live one. (4) In testing context, reads are an overlay: testing rows first, live underneath, live pinned at the seq the run started at. A proof reads live with no fixtures, what it wrote shadows live for that run only, and the run repeats within itself. (5) In live context the proxy never consults the TESTING database, so testing artifacts are invisible to all but the run that made them, by construction rather than by filtering. (6) Each run's testing rows carry its run id and are dropped at run end; the sleep cycle sweeps orphans. (7) A proof over live data asserts invariants, never snapshots; a tooth that needs an exact value writes its fixture into the overlay first. Until the per-box proxy exists, the same routing sits in the store door (db_domain) and moves into the proxy when it is built. WHY: a context the proof sets is a context a proof can forget; the runner is the one place every proof passes through. - akiendelllinux_orchestrator -amm

conflicts.text: A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, because even the Laws rest finally on the core principles. Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).
conflicts.ticket_says: The ticket says 'Find why ... reds and fix it so that the proof reseals green' without requiring that if the tooth (test case) changes, the decision be recorded in the same act as the change.
conflicts.why: The outline mandates 'a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6)'. The ticket's falsifier only requires the proof to reseal green, not that any decision be carried if the tooth is modified. A builder following the ticket exactly could change the tooth without recording the decision, violating both the corrosion requirement and preventing the system from learning why the tooth changed.
